# Platform settings · Billing

## Quota

<a id="QuotaForNewUser"></a>

### New user quota

Key `QuotaForNewUser` · Type int · Range 0– · Default `0`

Where: Platform settings › Billing › Quota

The quota a new account starts with, **granted once when it is created** and logged as a sign-up bonus. In quota units: 500,000 = $1 at the default quota per unit; the field also takes dollars. Accounts an organization creates for its members start at 0, and **changing it leaves existing balances alone**. 0 gives new users nothing until they top up or redeem a code.

Examples:

- `1000000` $2 of trial credit: about 119,000 output tokens of a $15 per million model sold at ratio 1.12.
- `0` New users can call nothing until they top up or redeem a code.

See also: [Quota per dollar](./site.md#QuotaPerUnit) · [Invitee sign-up bonus](./billing.md#QuotaForInvitee) · [Minimum top-up](./payment.md#PaymentMinAmount)

<a id="PreConsumedQuota"></a>

### Fixed pre-charge

Key `PreConsumedQuota` · Type int · Range 0– · Default `500` · rarely changed

Where: Platform settings › Billing › Quota

A fixed amount added to the up-front reservation of every token-priced request, on top of its estimated cost. The reservation (estimated input + reserved output tokens + this) is held from the balance or the API key's quota while the request runs and settled to the real cost when it ends, so it **decides who may start a request**, **never what is charged**. A balance below the reservation **is refused with insufficient quota**. In quota units: 500 = $0.001. Requests priced per call or per minute reserve their own price instead.

Examples:

- `500` The default. A request with 2,000 input tokens on a $3 / $15 per million model at ratio 1.12 holds 3,360 + 34,406 + 500 = 38,266 quota (about $0.077) until it settles.
- `50000` Every request needs $0.10 more than its estimate to start, so nearly empty balances are refused earlier.
- `0` Only the estimate is held: a balance just above it can still start a request.

See also: [Reserved output tokens](./billing.md#PreConsumedOutputTokens)

<a id="PreConsumedOutputTokens"></a>

### Reserved output tokens

Key `PreConsumedOutputTokens` · Type int · Range 0– · Default `4096` · rarely changed

Where: Platform settings › Billing › Quota

How many output tokens a token-priced request reserves up front, or the request's own max_tokens when smaller. Reserving its likely output keeps concurrent requests from **driving a balance far below zero**; the charge is **settled to the real usage** when the request ends. 0 reserves no output, only the input estimate and the fixed pre-charge.

Examples:

- `4096` The default. A $15 per million output model at ratio 1.12 reserves 4,096 x 8.4 = 34,406 quota (about $0.069) per request; a request with max_tokens 1,000 reserves 8,400.
- `32000` Long reasoning answers are covered up front: 32,000 x 8.4 = 268,800 quota (about $0.54) on the same model, so a balance below that cannot start a request.

See also: [Fixed pre-charge](./billing.md#PreConsumedQuota)

<a id="QuotaRemindEnabled"></a>

### Quota warning emails

Key `QuotaRemindEnabled` · Type bool · Default `true`

Where: Platform settings › Billing › Quota

Email users when their balance falls below the warning threshold, and again when it runs out. Each email is sent once; another goes out only after the balance has clearly recovered and fallen again. **Needs a mail service**. Users can turn the emails off or set their own threshold in their personal settings; **organization API keys never send them**. When off nobody gets them, and settlement skips the balance read the check needs.

See also: [Warning threshold](./billing.md#QuotaRemindThreshold)

<a id="QuotaRemindThreshold"></a>

### Warning threshold

Key `QuotaRemindThreshold` · Type int · Range 0– · Default `1000`

Where: Platform settings › Billing › Quota

The balance below which a user gets the "running low" email, in quota units (500,000 = $1). It is **the default for users who have not set their own threshold**. After an email the next one waits until the balance has gone back above the threshold plus 10% of it (or plus the fixed pre-charge, if larger) and fallen again. 0 **sends only the "used up" email**.

Examples:

- `1000` The default: the email goes out when $0.002 is left, about when the balance runs out.
- `5000000` Users hear when less than $10 is left; the next email comes only after the balance went back above $11 and fell again.

See also: [Quota warning emails](./billing.md#QuotaRemindEnabled) · [Quota per dollar](./site.md#QuotaPerUnit) · [Fixed pre-charge](./billing.md#PreConsumedQuota)

## Pricing

<a id="PaymentCostPercent"></a>

### Payment cost

Key `PaymentCostPercent` · Type percent · Unit % · Range 0–99.99 · Default `0`

Where: Platform settings › Billing › Pricing

What taking a payment costs the site, as a percentage of the amount: card fees and currency conversion. **Nobody is charged** it. It **only lowers the revenue** the price check and the margin figures compare channel costs with: net revenue = catalog price x the default group's ratio x (1 - payment cost). 0 counts payments as free.

Examples:

- `4` Card fee 3% plus 1% for currency conversion. With the default group at 1.12, $1 of catalog price brings in 1.12 x 0.96 = $1.0752.
- `0` Payments cost nothing: the price check compares channel costs with the full price.

See also: [Group ratio](./objects.md#user_group-ratio) · [Fee rate](./objects.md#channel-fee_rate)

Guide: [use/pricing_and_routing.md#the-price-check](../use/pricing_and_routing.md#the-price-check)

## Billing rules

<a id="EmptyResponseBillingEnabled"></a>

### Charge empty replies

Key `EmptyResponseBillingEnabled` · Type bool · Default `true`

Where: Platform settings › Billing › Billing rules

Charge token-priced requests whose reply has no output tokens for their input. When off such requests **are free**, although **the upstream may still bill you for the input**. Requests priced per call or per minute are charged either way, and a request with no tokens at all is never charged.

Examples:

- `true` An empty reply to 10,000 input tokens of a $3 per million model costs the user $0.03 at ratio 1.
- `false` The same request is free for the user; you still pay the upstream for the input.

<a id="ApproximateTokenEnabled"></a>

### Approximate token counting

Key `ApproximateTokenEnabled` · Type bool · Default `false` · rarely changed

Where: Platform settings › Billing › Billing rules

Count tokens locally as 0.38 tokens per byte of text instead of running the model's tokenizer. Local counts are used for the up-front reservation and when an upstream reply carries no usage; replies that report their usage are billed by it. It saves CPU on busy instances **at the cost of accuracy**, worst for text outside the Latin alphabet.

Examples:

- `true` 1,000 characters of English (1,000 bytes) count as 380 tokens; 1,000 Chinese characters (3,000 bytes) count as 1,140.

<a id="PriceSyncAutoApply"></a>

### Automatic price sync

Key `PriceSyncAutoApply` · Type enum · Default `increases`

Where: Platform settings › Billing › Billing rules

What the automatic price syncs (at startup, daily and when a channel is saved) write for models that already have a price. **New models are always added** and **locked prices never change**. Changes that are not written, and locked prices below the upstream price, are sent as notifications; review and apply them from the channel's price sync.

Values:

- `increases` Write increases, hold decreases: A price that went up is written at once, so you never sell below a new cost; a decrease waits for your review.
- `all` Write every change: The price table follows the upstream price lists both ways.
- `none` New models only: Every change to an existing price waits for your review.

Examples:

- `increases` An upstream raises a model's output from $10 to $12 per million: written at once. It cuts it to $8: the table keeps $10 and you are notified.
- `none` Both changes wait in the notification until you apply them.

## Periodic limit reset

<a id="QuotaResetTimezone"></a>

### Reset time zone

Key `QuotaResetTimezone` · Type string · Default `UTC`

Where: Platform settings › Billing › Periodic limit reset

The time zone whose midnight starts each daily, weekly and monthly limit period. It applies to API key period limits, organization budgets and member budgets. An IANA name; empty or unknown names **fall back to UTC**. Changing it **moves the boundary of the current period**.

Examples:

- `UTC` The default: daily limits reset at 00:00 UTC, which is 08:00 in Beijing.
- `Asia/Shanghai` Daily limits reset at 00:00 Beijing time, which is 16:00 UTC the day before.
- `America/New_York` Limits reset at local midnight through daylight saving time: 05:00 UTC in winter, 04:00 UTC in summer.

See also: [Week starts on](./billing.md#QuotaResetWeekStart)

<a id="QuotaResetWeekStart"></a>

### Week starts on

Key `QuotaResetWeekStart` · Type enum · Default `monday`

Where: Platform settings › Billing › Periodic limit reset

The day weekly limit periods start, at midnight in the reset time zone. Daily and monthly periods **are not affected**.

Values:

- `monday` Monday
- `sunday` Sunday

Examples:

- `monday` A weekly API key limit used up on Saturday is available again on Monday at 00:00.
- `sunday` The same limit comes back on Sunday at 00:00.

See also: [Reset time zone](./billing.md#QuotaResetTimezone)

## Invite rewards

<a id="InviteRewardEnabled"></a>

### Invite rewards

Key `InviteRewardEnabled` · Type bool · Default `true`

Where: Platform settings › Billing › Invite rewards

Pay invite rewards: sign-up bonuses for the inviter and the invitee, and the inviter's rebate on the first top-up. When off **none are paid and the site hides its invite entries**; who invited whom is still recorded.

See also: [Inviter sign-up bonus](./billing.md#QuotaForInviter) · [Invitee sign-up bonus](./billing.md#QuotaForInvitee) · [First top-up rebate type](./billing.md#InviterRewardType) · [First top-up rebate](./billing.md#InviterRewardValue)

<a id="QuotaForInviter"></a>

### Inviter sign-up bonus

Key `QuotaForInviter` · Type int · Range 0– · Default `0`

Where: Platform settings › Billing › Invite rewards

The quota an inviter gets each time someone signs up with their invite link or code. In quota units (500,000 = $1). 0 pays nothing at sign-up; **the first top-up rebate is set separately**.

Examples:

- `1000000` Each invited sign-up earns the inviter $2, whether or not the new user ever pays.
- `0` Inviters earn only the first top-up rebate, so fake sign-ups bring nothing.

See also: [Invite rewards](./billing.md#InviteRewardEnabled) · [Invitee sign-up bonus](./billing.md#QuotaForInvitee) · [First top-up rebate](./billing.md#InviterRewardValue)

<a id="QuotaForInvitee"></a>

### Invitee sign-up bonus

Key `QuotaForInvitee` · Type int · Range 0– · Default `0`

Where: Platform settings › Billing › Invite rewards

Extra quota a new user gets for signing up with an invite link or code, **on top of the new user quota**. In quota units (500,000 = $1). 0 gives invited users only the new user quota.

Examples:

- `500000` With the new user quota at 1,000,000 ($2), an invited user starts with $3.

See also: [Invite rewards](./billing.md#InviteRewardEnabled) · [New user quota](./billing.md#QuotaForNewUser) · [Inviter sign-up bonus](./billing.md#QuotaForInviter)

<a id="InviterRewardType"></a>

### First top-up rebate type

Key `InviterRewardType` · Type enum · Default `fixed`

Where: Platform settings › Billing › Invite rewards

How the inviter's rebate on an invited user's first paid top-up is counted: **a fixed quota** or a **percentage of the top-up**. The first top-up rebate sets the amount.

Values:

- `fixed` Fixed: The rebate is a quota amount, whatever the top-up.
- `percentage` Percentage: The rebate is a percentage of the quota the top-up bought.

See also: [First top-up rebate](./billing.md#InviterRewardValue)

<a id="InviterRewardValue"></a>

### First top-up rebate

Key `InviterRewardValue` · Type int · Range 0– · Default `0`

Where: Platform settings › Billing › Invite rewards

What an inviter earns when someone they invited makes a first paid top-up. For the fixed type it is quota units (500,000 = $1); for the percentage type a whole percentage from 0 to 100 of the quota bought. **Only the first paid top-up earns it**: later top-ups and redemption codes earn nothing. 0 **turns the rebate off**.

Examples:

- `10` Percentage: an invited user's first $50 top-up (25,000,000 quota) earns the inviter 2,500,000 quota, $5.
- `1000000` Fixed: the inviter gets $2 for the first top-up, whether it is $1 or $500.

See also: [First top-up rebate type](./billing.md#InviterRewardType) · [Invite rewards](./billing.md#InviteRewardEnabled) · [Top-up discounts](./payment.md#RechargeDiscount)
